transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because things haven’t been adding up for months. My sister’s appointments get moved, bills come in wrong, people say they forgot to call me back. Everyone keeps saying it’s just mistakes, but it doesn’t feel that way. It feels like information is being kept from me, like I’m being pushed out of decisions.
Do you believe someone is deliberately trying to keep information from you?

Yes. I mean… I can’t prove every single thing, but it’s been the same pattern for months. Appointments moved, bills wrong, calls not returned. People say it’s mistakes, but I don’t believe that. I think they’re keeping things from me and trying to push me out.
Do you feel certain that people are deliberately keeping information from you?

Yes. I do feel certain. It’s been the same thing for months now — appointments getting moved, bills showing up wrong, people “forgetting” to call me back. Maybe one or two things could be mistakes, but not all of it. I know they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.
Is it possible at all that you might be mistaken about people deliberately keeping information from you?

I suppose anything is possible, but… no, I don’t think I’m mistaken. Not after months of the same things happening — appointments moved, bills wrong, people not calling back. They keep saying it’s mistakes, but it doesn’t feel like mistakes to me. It feels deliberate.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, not voices like that.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?
I don’t know… not really. I still do some things. Maybe I’m less enthusiastic than I used to be, but I haven’t thought about it much.
Do other people ever tell you that this belief is not true or doesn’t make sense?

Yes. They say I’m “reading into things,” or that offices make mistakes. My sister especially… she acts like it doesn’t add up. But it’s been months of the same pattern—appointments moved, bills wrong, people not calling me back. At some point it stops looking like mistakes.
Have you had the feeling that someone else is controlling your thoughts?

No… not controlling my thoughts, exactly. It’s more that people are keeping things from me and trying to steer what happens—like with my sister’s appointments and bills. Everyone says it’s mistakes, but it’s been going on too long.
Have you heard voices speaking to you when no one else is around?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices like that when I’m alone.
Do you believe anything impossible is happening to you, such as people using special powers or technology to influence events around you?

No… I wouldn’t say special powers or anything like that. It’s more… people controlling information. My sister’s appointments getting moved, bills being wrong, calls not returned. Everyone says it’s mistakes, but it feels too consistent. I know they’re keeping me out of decisions somehow.
Has this been making it hard for you to work or manage your usual day-to-day responsibilities?

A little, I guess. I’m still getting things done, at home and at work. But family meetings have gotten… tense. And at work I’ve had a couple awkward conversations because I pushed harder than I used to over routine mistakes. People react differently to me now.
Do you ever feel that your thoughts are being broadcast so that other people can know what you are thinking?

No… not like people can hear my thoughts. It’s more that they keep information from me. Like with my sister’s appointments, bills being wrong, people not calling back… it’s been going on for months. Everyone says it’s just mistakes, but I know I’m being pushed out of decisions.
Do you ever feel that outside forces are putting thoughts into your mind?

No… I don’t think anyone is putting thoughts in my head. It’s not like that. It’s more what I’ve said—things keep happening with my sister’s appointments, bills, calls not being returned… and it’s too consistent. I know they’re keeping information from me somehow.
Aside from people keeping information from you, do you have any other unusual beliefs that others say are not true?

Not really other things, no. It’s mostly this pattern with my sister—appointments being moved, bills suddenly wrong, people not calling me back. Everyone keeps saying it’s ordinary mistakes, but after months of it… I don’t believe that. It feels like they’re trying to keep me out of decisions.
During this period, have you had times of feeling unusually high or unusually depressed?
I don’t think so. I mean… I’ve been stressed, sure, and upset about all of this, but not unusually high or really depressed like that.
Have you seen things that other people could not see?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t seen anything that other people couldn’t see.
Have people close to you noticed that you’ve become emotionally flat or less expressive than you used to be?
I’m not sure. I don’t think anyone’s said that to me directly. Maybe I’ve been quieter, but… I wouldn’t say flat.
Before these problems with your sister started, were you generally someone who often distrusted other people’s motives?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I was suspicious of everyone, if that’s what you mean. I kept to myself some, but I didn’t think about it that way.
Have other people told you that your speech has been hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another?
No, not really. I mean… I don’t think anyone’s told me that. I can be careful with what I say, but I don’t think I jump around like that.
Did this start very suddenly, within a day or two?
No… not within a day or two. It’s been more gradual, I guess. Around 11 months now, since my sister’s health got worse and I had to get involved with her care.

There is clear conviction despite reassurance from others, but no hallucinations, thought insertion/broadcasting/control, bizarre delusions, disorganized speech, negative symptoms, or prominent mood episodes. Functioning is only mildly affected, which supports persistent delusional disorder over schizophrenia, acute polymorphic psychosis, or paranoid personality disorder.
